claims.claim: A five-sentence 1980 letter by Porter and Jick in the New England Journal of Medicine reported only four cases of well-documented addiction among 11,882 hospitalized patients who received narcotics.
claims.episode_span: a 1980 letter in the New England Journal of Medicine reporting only four cases of addiction among nearly 12,000 hospitalized patients was widely cited as reassurance
claims.source_title: Addiction Rare in Patients Treated with Narcotics - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: Although there were 11,882 patients who received at least one narcotic preparation, there were only four cases of reasonably well documented addiction in patients who had no history of addiction.

claims.claim: Purdue's sales force told physicians that the risk of addiction from OxyContin was less than one percent.
claims.episode_span: Detailers distributed charts and videos stating that addiction occurred in “less than one percent” of patients
claims.supporting_quote: Purdue trained its sales representatives to convey to doctors that the risk of addiction from OxyContin was "less than one percent."

claims.claim: In June 2024 the U.S. Supreme Court (Harrington v. Purdue Pharma) held that the Bankruptcy Code does not authorize discharging claims against a nondebtor without the consent of affected claimants.
claims.episode_span: was struck down by the United States Supreme Court in June 2024, which held that bankruptcy courts cannot release third parties from claims without the consent of those suing
claims.source_title: Harrington v. Purdue Pharma L.P. - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: The bankruptcy code does not authorize a release and injunction that, as part of a plan of reorganization under Chapter 11, effectively seek to discharge claims against a nondebtor without the consent of affected claimants.

claims.claim: Under the Purdue bankruptcy plan approved in November 2025, the Sacklers must contribute up to $7 billion over 15 years.
claims.episode_span: under the plan confirmed in November 2025 the Sacklers pay up to roughly $7 billion over fifteen years
claims.source_title: Judge approves opioid settlement for Purdue Pharma and Sackler family members who own the company - STAT
claims.supporting_quote: The Sacklers must contribute up to $7 billion over 15 years. Most of the money will go to government entities to fight the opioid crisis, which has been linked to 900,000 deaths in the U.S. since 1999.

claims.claim: The 2025 plan's releases of the Sacklers are consensual/opt-in: claimants who do not opt in keep their right to sue members of the Sackler family.
claims.episode_span: the releases are opt-in — creditors who opt out keep the right to sue
claims.source_title: Purdue Pharma's $7.4 Billion Chapter 11 Plan Formally Approved | Knobbe Martens
claims.supporting_quote: under the current agreement, entities and claimants that do not opt into the payments will maintain their right to sue members of the Sackler family

claims.claim: Purdue Pharma filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on September 15, 2019.
claims.episode_span: Purdue Pharma filed for bankruptcy in September 2019; the settlements that followed, including the Justice Department resolution announced in October 2020, exceeded $8 billion.
claims.supporting_quote: Purdue filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on September 15, 2019, in New York City.

claims.claim: Purdue reached a settlement announced in October 2020 potentially worth about $8.3 billion.
claims.episode_span: including the Justice Department resolution announced in October 2020, exceeded $8 billion
claims.supporting_quote: On October 21, 2020, it was reported that Purdue had reached a settlement potentially worth US$8.3 billion

claims.claim: The FDA approved OxyContin in 1995 without long-term studies or an assessment of its addictive potential.
claims.episode_span: Regulators at the FDA, operating under 1990s standards that accepted company-submitted studies of short duration, approved the drug in December 1995 for moderate-to-severe pain.
claims.supporting_quote: Purdue managed to get it approved in 1995, even though no long-term studies and no assessment of its addictive capabilities had been conducted.
